039dedac5908f8105b6934cbb9b47e4af2e3ced8:
**Paid Time Off (PTO) Accrual for Full‑Time Employees**  
Full‑time employees accrue PTO at a rate of 1.25 days per month of continuous service, resulting in a total of 15 days of PTO per calendar year. Accrual begins on the first day of employment and is prorated for any partial months of service. Unused PTO may be carried over to the following year up to a maximum of 5 days, provided the employee remains in active status. Additional PTO may be granted at the discretion of management in accordance with applicable collective bargaining agreements or special company programs.
a61b700e4a2f1b0b8b19b74b27d73e4c16e74a4e:
**Paid Time Off (PTO) Carryover Policy**  
Employees may carry over a maximum of **5 days (40 hours)** of unused PTO into the following calendar year, provided the balance does not exceed the employee’s annual accrual rate. Any accrued PTO in excess of the 5‑day limit will be forfeited on December 31, unless a written waiver is approved by the HR Director in accordance with applicable state law. Carryover PTO must be used by **June 30** of the subsequent year; any remaining balance after that date will be forfeited. This policy applies to all regular full‑time and part‑time employees unless otherwise specified in a collective bargaining agreement or individual employment contract.
e52108537d7ca3838a9579ba7610813821bf7af7:
**Paid Time Off (PTO) Request Procedure**  
Employees must submit a written request for any PTO of two consecutive days or longer at least **ten (10) business days** prior to the first day of the requested leave. Requests submitted with less than ten business days’ notice will be considered only in cases of emergency or unforeseen circumstances and may be denied at the discretion of the employee’s manager. All PTO requests must be entered into the company’s time‑off management system and approved by the employee’s direct supervisor before the leave can be taken.
23293c8f2b9b6211c499d986735a782ee7869d9a:
**Paid Time Off (PTO) Request Procedure – Extended Leave**  
Employees must submit a written request for any consecutive PTO period of five (5) business days or more at least **four (4) weeks** prior to the first day of the requested leave. The request must be entered into the HRIS system and approved by the employee’s direct supervisor and the department’s HR representative. Failure to meet the four‑week notice requirement may result in the request being denied or placed on a wait‑list, subject to operational needs. Exceptions for unforeseen circumstances will be considered on a case‑by‑case basis in accordance with the company’s emergency leave policy.
d3025089935458aec8a6f0d18f5dd7bfed2a0c47:
**Sick‑Leave Notification and Approval Policy**

Employees must notify their immediate supervisor of an unscheduled absence due to illness as soon as practicable, but no later than the start of the scheduled workday. The supervisor’s acknowledgment of the notification constitutes the required approval for the sick leave; no additional managerial sign‑off is needed. If the employee is unable to reach their supervisor directly, they may contact the designated department‑wide on‑call manager or the HR hotline, after which the supervisor will be informed promptly. All sick‑leave requests must be documented in the company’s time‑keeping system within 24 hours of the employee’s return.
7bf1fd782b0d3ccb473495e08981ce6ea651e22a:
**Unused Paid Time Off (PTO) Upon Separation**  
When an employee voluntarily resigns or is terminated for cause, any accrued but unused PTO will be paid out in a lump‑sum as part of the final paycheck, provided the employee has completed all required exit procedures and returned all company property. The payout will be calculated based on the employee’s regular rate of pay at the time of separation and will be subject to applicable taxes and withholdings. Employees who are terminated without cause or who leave due to retirement will receive the same PTO payout under the same conditions. No PTO will be carried over or transferred to another employee after the termination date.
e357b402ae2129285f0268ea709fd08f726891e5:
**Paid Company Holidays**

The Company observes a total of **eleven (11) paid holidays each calendar year**. These holidays are designated by the Company and include all federally recognized public holidays, as well as additional days specified in the annual holiday calendar distributed at the beginning of each fiscal year. Employees will receive their regular rate of pay for each designated holiday, provided they are scheduled to work on that day or are otherwise eligible under the Company’s attendance policy. The holiday schedule may be adjusted at the discretion of management, with any changes communicated to all staff at least thirty (30) days in advance.
b8fb9f0c4c2679e5d75ee02b35d184818030b854:
**Paid Time Off (PTO) Accrual for Part‑Time Employees**  
Part‑time employees are eligible to accrue PTO on a pro‑rated basis according to the number of hours worked each pay period. Accrual rates are calculated by dividing the full‑time annual PTO entitlement by the standard full‑time weekly hours (40) and then multiplying by the employee’s regularly scheduled weekly hours. PTO accrual begins on the first day of employment and is reflected in each paycheck’s earnings statement. Unused accrued PTO may be carried over to the next calendar year in accordance with the company’s PTO carry‑over limits.
b8f90d96e82904a3b36ef4d4f0532be43fa760e8:
**Hybrid Work Schedule Policy**

Hybrid‑eligible employees are required to be present on‑site for a minimum of **two (2) full workdays per calendar week**. The specific days may be selected by the employee in coordination with their manager, provided that core business hours (10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.) are covered and any departmental scheduling constraints are met. Exceptions or alternative arrangements must be approved in writing by the employee’s supervisor and HR.
8222a0bd2e9cf8ff5d2a77035651a66df55aab2f:
**Home Office Stipend Policy**

1. **Eligibility:** All full‑time employees who have been with the company for a minimum of 90 consecutive days and who are required to perform at least 50 % of their duties remotely are eligible to receive a home office stipend. Contractors, part‑time staff, and employees on temporary or probationary assignments are not covered by this stipend.

2. **Stipend Amount:** Eligible employees will receive a quarterly stipend of $250 to offset home‑office expenses, payable with the regular payroll cycle. The stipend is subject to annual review and may be adjusted based on inflation or changes to the company’s remote‑work budget.
a6ff7426379375bbd08c4dbf40a094c994a01966:
**Remote Employee Core Working Hours**

All remote employees are required to be available for core working hours each workday from **9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. (local time of the employee’s primary work location)**. During this period, employees must be reachable via company‑approved communication channels (e‑mail, instant messaging, and video conferencing) and be prepared to attend scheduled meetings, respond to inquiries, and collaborate with team members. Exceptions to these core hours may be granted only with prior written approval from the employee’s manager and Human Resources.
48477cedcf5133fb0ab7347b0fa30f11b546ce4c:
**Remote Work – International Locations**  
Employees may perform remote work from a location outside the United States only with prior written approval from both their direct manager and the Global Mobility team. The employee must maintain compliance with all applicable tax, immigration, and labor laws of the host country, and the company reserves the right to require a temporary or permanent return to an authorized work location if legal or operational concerns arise. All international remote work arrangements must be documented in a Remote Work Agreement, signed by the employee, manager, and HR, and are subject to periodic review.
2a070ac60b1061e8f60ef6c1e5c2e3127c6489aa:
**Remote Access Policy – VPN Requirement**  
All employees who access company systems, applications, or data from off‑site locations must do so through the corporate Virtual Private Network (VPN). The VPN provides encrypted connections that meet our security standards and ensures compliance with data protection regulations. Exceptions are limited to approved third‑party tools that have been expressly authorized by the IT Security team in writing. Failure to use the VPN when required constitutes a violation of the Acceptable Use Policy and may result in disciplinary action.
7d28e72aca3f9125fc3cc16d0e49ddf2cdc241eb:
**Access to Confidential Company Data on Personal Devices**  
Employees are prohibited from storing, transmitting, or accessing confidential company data on personal mobile phones, tablets, or any non‑company‑issued devices unless expressly authorized by the Information Security Office and protected by approved, company‑managed mobile device management (MDM) solutions. All confidential information must be accessed only through company‑provided hardware or secure, company‑controlled virtual environments that enforce encryption, authentication, and remote wipe capabilities. Any violation of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.
5354b7122d4e4947ce9b7f8708237886ac8cafc1:
**Remote‑Eligibility, Hybrid, and On‑Site Designation Policy**

1. The determination of a position’s work‑location classification (remote‑eligible, hybrid, or on‑site) is made by the department’s functional manager in consultation with the Human Resources Business Partner, based on operational needs, job responsibilities, and applicable regulatory or security requirements.  
2. The final approval of the classification is granted by the Senior Director of People Operations, who ensures consistency with company‑wide remote‑work guidelines and budgetary constraints.  
3. Any changes to an employee’s work‑location status must be documented in the employee’s record and communicated in writing by the HR Business Partner.
d5fd0fe7b3cf3f47d2bba8e4ed991d5e3de8472b:
**Remote Work Equipment Provision Policy**

The Company shall furnish each eligible remote employee with the following standard equipment: a laptop computer pre‑configured with required security software, a dual‑monitor setup, an ergonomic keyboard and mouse, and a high‑speed broadband internet stipend up to the monthly cap specified in the Remote Work Allowance Schedule. Additional peripherals (e.g., headset, webcam, docking station) may be provided upon written request and manager approval, subject to budget availability. All equipment remains the property of the Company and must be returned upon termination of employment or reassignment to on‑site duties.
cecd5d883a3774a337da33b4517127ff893ebae5:
**Expense Report Submission Deadline**  
All employees must submit completed expense reports for incurred costs within **15 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Reports submitted after this period will be considered late and may be subject to denial or delayed reimbursement, unless an exception is granted in writing by the employee’s manager and the Finance Department. Employees are responsible for ensuring that all supporting documentation (receipts, approvals, etc.) is attached to the report at the time of submission.
a8ced57b51247e252333599d9d7c0af625086007:
**Reimbursable Expenses – Alcoholic Beverages**  
The Company does not consider the purchase of alcoholic beverages to be a reimbursable business expense.  Any costs incurred for alcohol, whether at client meetings, conferences, or employee events, are the sole responsibility of the employee and will not be submitted for reimbursement.  Exceptions may be granted only with prior written approval from the Finance Director and must be documented in accordance with the “Entertainment and Hospitality” expense guidelines.  All other legitimate business expenses must be submitted using the standard expense reporting procedures.
09be8f902aa79a0ba2d76b36a44ee4964444e785:
**Domestic Travel – Meal Reimbursement**  
The Company will reimburse employees for meals incurred while traveling domestically at a maximum of **$55 per day**. This daily cap applies to the combined cost of breakfast, lunch, and dinner and is non‑cumulative; any amount exceeding the cap will not be reimbursed. Receipts must be submitted with the travel expense report to receive reimbursement up to the stated limit.
00f1ffec46e627dfcde9c14d7ea1eafd5aee295f:
**International Travel – Daily Meal Reimbursement Cap**  
The Company will reimburse employees for meals incurred while on authorized international travel up to a maximum of **USD 75 per calendar day**. This cap applies to the total amount of breakfast, lunch, dinner, and incidental meals consumed each day, regardless of the destination. Receipts must be submitted in accordance with the Travel Expense Reporting Procedure, and any amount exceeding the daily limit will not be reimbursed. Exceptions may be granted only with prior written approval from the employee’s manager and the Finance Department.
f0bda072bc454767b24d64f4ec3f765d2fe1e329:
**Expense Documentation Policy – Minimum Receipt Requirement**  
All business-related expenses must be supported by original documentation to be eligible for reimbursement. A receipt is required for any single expense of $25 or more; expenses under $25, such as a $20 purchase, may be reimbursed with a written explanation of the expense in lieu of a receipt. The written explanation must include the date, vendor name, purpose of the expense, and the exact amount incurred. Employees should retain any available proof of purchase (e‑mail confirmation, credit‑card statement, or similar) and submit it with the expense report when possible.
ae3982f3f6e95cd87d3a9c0e3b44eb533e938cc2:
**Expense Report Approval Requirements**

All expense reports totaling **$500.01 up to $1,000** must be reviewed and approved by the employee’s direct supervisor **and** the Finance Department’s Expense Coordinator before reimbursement can be processed. The employee must attach itemized receipts and a completed expense justification form to the submission. Failure to obtain both approvals will result in the expense report being returned for correction.
f444600cedae353c8629bedbc1cc1fbfe1765ae0:
**Travel Booking Policy – Hotel Accommodations**  
Employees are required to use the company‑approved travel portal for all lodging reservations related to business travel. Booking hotels outside the portal is prohibited unless a pre‑approved exception is granted in writing by the Travel Manager. Exceptions may be considered only for circumstances such as limited availability, special rates, or safety concerns, and must be documented in the travel request prior to departure. Non‑compliant bookings will not be reimbursed and may be subject to disciplinary action.
907ad1e5b14b7ce197182175cb9dace4e40cfd58:
**Reimbursement Timing Policy**

Reimbursements for approved expense claims will be processed within **10 business days** after the claim has been approved by the appropriate manager and the Finance department has received all required documentation. The payment will be issued via the employee’s regular payroll or direct deposit method, as specified in the employee’s payroll profile. If additional information is needed, the claim will be returned to the employee for clarification, and the processing clock will restart upon receipt of the requested items. Employees will be notified by email when their reimbursement has been completed.
863ff4339a7f379f512e139cf2351cee9d93b907:
**Harassment Reporting Procedure**  
All employees who experience or witness harassment must promptly report the concern to their immediate supervisor or, if the supervisor is involved or the employee feels uncomfortable doing so, to the Human Resources Department at hr@company.com or the designated Ethics Hotline (1‑800‑555‑HELP). Reports may also be submitted directly to the Chief Compliance Officer or any member of the senior leadership team. The company will investigate all reports confidentially, protect against retaliation, and take appropriate corrective action in accordance with our anti‑harassment policy.
2d6e4209c0bf56b65b2e10da8b5937b2c9e85414:
**Retaliation Prohibition and Good‑Faith Reporting**  
The Company strictly prohibits any form of retaliation against employees who, in good faith, report a concern, regardless of the eventual outcome of the investigation. Employees who make a report in good faith are protected from adverse employment actions, including termination, demotion, reassignment, or any other punitive measure, even if the concern is later determined to be unfounded. Any retaliation will be treated as a separate violation of this policy and may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination. This protection applies to all reporting channels, including the Ethics Hotline, direct manager, Human Resources, or any designated compliance officer.
029f37078b95d4a92f033d8fb8ab5116480cfc69:
**Side‑Business Disclosure Policy**  
All employees must disclose any external business activities, including side businesses operated on weekends, that could present a conflict of interest, affect job performance, or involve the use of Company resources. Disclosure must be submitted in writing to the Human Resources Department using the “External Activity Disclosure Form” within five (5) business days of commencing the activity. Failure to disclose a qualifying side business may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
2de8eb931da3413940d25a332978a283842d6674:
**Disciplinary Process for Code of Conduct Violations**

1. **Investigation:** Upon receipt of a suspected Code of Conduct violation, the Human Resources department, in coordination with the employee’s manager, will conduct a prompt, impartial investigation to gather all relevant facts and documentation.  
2. **Preliminary Findings:** If the investigation reveals sufficient evidence of a violation, the employee will be notified in writing of the preliminary findings and invited to provide a response or additional information within five business days.  
3. **Determination and Action:** A disciplinary committee, comprising HR, legal, and senior management representatives, will review the investigation report and the employee’s response. Based on the severity and frequency of the violation, the committee may impose one or more of the following actions: verbal warning, written reprimand, suspension (with or without pay), demotion, or termination of employment.  
4. **Documentation and Appeal:** All decisions, supporting evidence, and the rationale for the chosen disciplinary action will be documented in the employee’s personnel file. The employee has the right to appeal the decision in writing within ten business days, after which the appeal will be reviewed by a senior executive not previously involved in the case.
24cdf2d6f6a1bb1d1328b480b52ae8d84ab16033:
**Compensation Confidentiality Policy**  
All employees must treat compensation information as strictly confidential. Disclosure of any coworker’s salary, wages, bonuses, or other remuneration details to clients, vendors, or any external parties is prohibited. Violations of this confidentiality requirement may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. This policy applies to all forms of communication, including verbal, written, and electronic messages.
23145d40861f4933e82c10c243ab29a0bd265f31:
**Confidentiality Obligation After Employment Termination**  
All employees retain an ongoing duty to protect the Company’s confidential and proprietary information, including trade secrets, client data, and internal business strategies, for an indefinite period following the termination of their employment, whether voluntary or involuntary. This obligation survives the end of the employment relationship and is enforceable regardless of the manner or timing of the employee’s departure. Any unauthorized disclosure, use, or retention of such information after separation will be considered a breach of this policy and may result in legal action and/or financial liability.
12fa5ac1b3d191448502b14a68887b11d055574d:
**Paid Parental Leave**

Eligible employees are entitled to **up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave** for the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child. The leave may be taken continuously or intermittently within the first 12 months following the child’s arrival, subject to manager approval and compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations. Employees must submit a written request for parental leave at least 30 days prior to the anticipated start date, accompanied by appropriate documentation. Pay during parental leave is provided at the employee’s regular base salary rate and is not counted against accrued vacation or sick leave balances.
1df2ffd5e5951a7c9d64ad1f644cd9c0c09a3500:
**Parental Leave Timing Policy**

Employees must submit a written request for parental leave to the Human Resources Department no later than 30 calendar days prior to the anticipated start date of the leave. The leave must be taken within 12 months of the birth, adoption, or legal guardianship of the child, unless an extension is approved in writing by HR due to extenuating circumstances. Failure to provide the required notice or to commence the leave within the 12‑month window may result in the forfeiture of the employee’s parental leave entitlement.
159448bc44abe00f8fef9c73c61799caa54b3a6f:
**Parental Leave – Splitting Leave Periods**  
Employees may elect to divide their eligible parental leave into multiple, non‑consecutive blocks, provided that each block is a minimum of one full workweek and the total combined duration does not exceed the statutory entitlement. Requests to split leave must be submitted in writing to Human Resources at least 30 days prior to the start of the first requested block, and each subsequent block must be approved by the employee’s manager and HR. The total number of split blocks may not exceed three, and any unused portion of the entitlement will be forfeited if not taken within the applicable leave window as defined in the employee handbook.
fc22d9e7acfa875223c1a23cc6d5fc12f5a4d355:
**Family and Medical Leave – Dual‑Employee Households**  
Employees who are married to, or in a domestic partnership with, another eligible employee are each entitled to the full statutory leave entitlement. Each spouse may independently request up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job‑protected leave per qualifying event, provided the employee meets the standard eligibility criteria (30 days of service and 1,250 hours worked in the preceding 12 months). The leave periods are not coordinated or shared; both employees may take their full 12 weeks concurrently or at different times, subject to operational needs and manager approval. All other provisions of the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and company policy apply equally to each employee.
1bb76a227cdac882ef3be1a2aeb2f70d4c0a3e67:
**Parental Leave Notice Requirements**  
Employees intending to take parental leave must submit a written request to the Human Resources Department at least **30 calendar days** prior to the anticipated start date of the leave. The request must include the expected start and end dates, the type of parental leave being taken, and any supporting documentation required by law or company policy. In cases of unforeseen circumstances or medical emergencies, employees should notify HR as soon as practicable, and the company will consider the request on a case‑by‑case basis. Failure to provide the required notice may result in a delay or denial of the requested leave.
a85e353693ff85e4f2c557b8e9050d4dc7ba13f9:
**Health Benefits During Parental Leave**  
Employees who are on approved parental leave retain continuous coverage under the company’s health insurance plan, provided that they remain enrolled in the plan and continue to pay any required employee contributions on schedule. The employer will continue to pay its share of premiums for the duration of the leave, up to the maximum leave period permitted by law or company policy. Should an employee’s leave extend beyond the standard entitlement, the employee must elect to continue coverage under COBRA or a comparable continuation option, and any additional costs will be the employee’s responsibility. All other benefit eligibility criteria (e.g., deductibles, co‑pays, and network access) remain unchanged during the leave period.
e15fb3c54a706162685f9a98f7e68c4f880d0d07:
**Parental Leave Eligibility for Part‑Time Employees**  
All regular part‑time employees who have completed at least 12 months of continuous service with the company are eligible to take parental leave on the same terms and conditions as full‑time employees, prorated to reflect their scheduled work hours. Eligibility is based on the employee’s average weekly hours over the preceding 12‑month period, not on the total number of hours worked per week. Part‑time employees may receive parental leave benefits proportionally to their work schedule, and the duration of leave will be calculated on a full‑time equivalent basis and adjusted accordingly. Any required documentation and notice must be submitted in accordance with the standard parental‑leave request procedures.
e0c2501463a2008c0dcce41bc5950fe27af5bbb9:
**Benefits Enrollment Deadline for New Hires**  
All newly hired employees must complete their benefits enrollment within **30 calendar days** of their official start date. The enrollment period begins on the first day of employment and ends at 11:59 p.m. on the 30th day thereafter. Failure to enroll within this timeframe will result in the employee being ineligible for that plan year’s benefits, and enrollment will not be possible until the next open enrollment period, unless a qualifying life event occurs. Employees are encouraged to review the Benefits Guide and submit the required enrollment forms promptly to avoid loss of coverage.
5a8e1609c2c167914b423f76a62a028e29e8d2fb:
**Benefits Effective Date Policy**  
All newly hired employees become eligible for company-sponsored benefits on the first day of the month following the completion of their 30‑day introductory period, provided that enrollment forms have been submitted and approved by the Benefits Administration. If the employee’s start date falls on the first day of a month, coverage will commence on the first day of the next month after the 30‑day period is satisfied. Employees who enroll after the initial enrollment window will have coverage begin on the first day of the month following the date their enrollment is processed. The HR Department will issue a confirmation notice indicating the exact effective date of benefits for each employee.
8fb3849220442aa158a98f9a2756bbb37cf8e167:
**Open Enrollment Period**  
Open enrollment for employee benefits will occur annually during the first two weeks of November, beginning at 12:00 a.m. on Monday, November 4, and concluding at 11:59 p.m. on Sunday, November 18. All eligible employees must submit their benefit selections, changes, or cancellations within this window; any modifications submitted after the deadline will be deferred to the next enrollment cycle. Exceptions for qualifying life events (e.g., marriage, birth, loss of other coverage) are handled through the Special Enrollment process and are not subject to the open enrollment dates.
f8c4fdb5d310beb2c91da5601867de752ba46423:
**Benefits Election Changes – Qualifying Life Events**  
Employees may modify their benefits elections outside the annual open‑enrollment period only when a qualifying life event occurs. The birth of a child is a qualifying life event; therefore, an employee who has a baby may adjust health, dental, vision, flexible‑spending, and dependent‑care elections. The employee must submit a completed Benefits Election Change Form, accompanied by appropriate documentation (e.g., birth certificate or hospital record), to Human Resources within 30 calendar days of the birth. Changes will become effective on the first day of the month following HR’s acceptance of the request. Failure to submit the required documentation within the 30‑day window will forfeit the opportunity to change elections until the next open‑enrollment period.
4e8b5751b395f50ae6149e7248aae929a16de561:
**401(k) Matching Policy**

The Company will match employee elective deferrals to the 401(k) plan at a rate of 100 % on the first 3 % of eligible compensation and 50 % on the next 2 % of eligible compensation, for a total maximum match of 4 % of an employee’s annual compensation. Matching contributions are made each pay period following the receipt of the employee’s deferral election and are subject to the vesting schedule outlined in the Plan Document. Employees must be eligible under the plan’s participation requirements and must submit a valid deferral election to receive the match. The Company reserves the right to amend or discontinue the matching formula, provided that any changes will be communicated in writing at least 30 days prior to the effective date.
5d5b7d5614b19025d860a83ed269ef0ec4963d3d:
**401(k) Automatic Enrollment Policy**  
All eligible full‑time employees are automatically enrolled in the company 401(k) retirement plan on the first regular payroll date following the completion of their 30‑day introductory employment period. Eligibility requires that the employee be at least 21 years of age and have completed the required onboarding documentation, including the benefits election form. If an employee wishes to decline enrollment, they must submit a written opt‑out request to Human Resources within ten (10) business days of the automatic enrollment date; otherwise, contributions will be deducted from each subsequent paycheck at the default contribution rate of 3% of eligible earnings. The automatic enrollment will remain in effect until the employee elects a different contribution rate, changes their investment selections, or formally withdraws from the plan in accordance with the plan’s termination procedures.
7b77d45903ac9a9d0e88c37078f4c751f8a6c150:
**Health Savings Account (HSA) Employer Contribution Policy**

The Company will contribute a fixed amount of **$1,200 per calendar year** to each eligible employee’s Health Savings Account, deposited in equal quarterly installments of $300 on the last business day of each quarter. Contributions are made only to employees who are enrolled in a qualified high‑deductible health plan and who have an active HSA account on the first day of the quarter. The Company’s contribution is a non‑taxable benefit and is not considered wages for payroll or tax reporting purposes. If an employee’s employment terminates for any reason, the Company will cease all future HSA contributions as of the termination date, and any contributions already deposited remain the employee’s property.
ba84f287639238423da1300ddad1aba59aa85971:
**Spouse Eligibility Documentation**  
To add a spouse to the Company’s health insurance plan, the employee must submit the following documents within 30 days of the qualifying life event: (1) a completed **Spouse Enrollment Form** signed by both the employee and the spouse; (2) a **valid government‑issued photo ID** for the spouse (e.g., driver’s license, passport, or state ID); (3) an **official marriage certificate** or, for common‑law partners, a **domestic partnership affidavit** accompanied by proof of cohabitation (e.g., joint lease, utility bills, or joint tax return). All documents must be provided to the Benefits Administration team either electronically through the HR portal or in person at the HR office. Failure to submit the required documentation within the 30‑day window may result in the loss of eligibility for that plan year.
db0dbcce2b1c0307aca802c9b8e6a8e3432e9326:
**Dress Code Policy**

All employees are expected to maintain a professional appearance that reflects the company’s standards and the nature of their role. Business‑formal attire (e.g., suits, dress shirts, blouses, dress shoes) is required for client‑facing positions and during formal meetings; business‑casual attire (e.g., collared shirts, slacks, skirts, dresses, closed‑toed shoes) is acceptable for internal office work and non‑client days. Clothing must be clean, neat, and free of offensive graphics, slogans, or excessive wear. Exceptions for religious, cultural, or medical reasons may be granted upon request to Human Resources.
e0d0a3665f975f69fb989262fc040e9c817dea02:
**Department Transfer Request Procedure**

Employees wishing to transfer to a different department must submit a written Transfer Request Form to their immediate supervisor no later than the 15th of the month preceding the desired effective date. The supervisor will review the request for operational feasibility and forward the completed form, along with any supporting documentation, to the Human Resources Business Partner within five business days. HR will evaluate the request against current staffing needs, skill‑match criteria, and any applicable internal mobility guidelines, and will communicate a decision to the employee and both the current and prospective department managers within ten business days of receipt. All approved transfers will be coordinated with payroll and IT to ensure a seamless transition on the agreed start date.
769c2def3d83d48376234cf4167967710e3a35b6:
**Internal Job Posting Application Procedure**

1. Employees interested in an internal vacancy must submit a formal application through the company’s internal career portal no later than the closing date indicated on the posting.  
2. The application shall include an updated résumé, a completed Internal Candidate Form, and a brief statement of interest, all uploaded to the designated posting page.  
3. Upon submission, the employee’s current manager must be notified electronically and provide a written endorsement within three business days; the endorsement is required for the application to be considered.  
4. The HR Recruitment Team will acknowledge receipt of the application within two business days and will communicate any further steps, including interviews or assessments, directly to the candidate.
294cbf90cafe6afb214004762c803821f4b8f193:
**Tuition Reimbursement Policy**

The Company provides tuition reimbursement for eligible employees who enroll in approved academic courses related to their current job responsibilities or a defined career path within the organization. Reimbursement is limited to 100% of tuition costs up to $5,000 per calendar year, provided the employee maintains a minimum grade of “B” (or 3.0 GPA) and submits all required documentation within 30 days of course completion. Employees must have completed at least six months of continuous service before becoming eligible, and any reimbursement will be subject to repayment if the employee voluntarily separates from the Company within 12 months of receiving the benefit. The Human Resources Department administers the program and may adjust limits or eligibility criteria at its discretion.
3d5af83d6bbd539a4c1c6272e39415afe3140efd:
**Office Pet Policy**

1. Pets are not permitted in company office spaces, including workstations, conference rooms, break areas, and restrooms, unless a specific exemption has been granted in writing by the Facilities Manager and approved by Human Resources.  
2. Exceptions may be made for service animals that meet the legal definition of a disability‑related assistance animal, provided the employee submits appropriate documentation and the animal does not pose a health or safety risk.  
3. Employees who violate this policy may be asked to remove the animal from the premises and may be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the Employee Conduct Guidelines.  
4. For any questions or to request an exemption, employees should submit a written request to HR at least five business days prior to the intended date.
c73575fe347a6f031cc28983edf5954b4cf2054f:
**Parking Pass Allocation Policy**

1. All employees eligible for a parking pass must submit a completed **Parking Pass Request Form** through the HR portal under the “Facilities & Services” section.  
2. Requests are processed on a first‑come, first‑served basis each month; approvals are communicated via email within five business days of submission.  
3. Approved employees will receive a temporary pass to be exchanged for a permanent pass at the Facilities Management office, located on the ground floor, during normal business hours (8:00 AM – 5:00 PM).  
4. Parking passes are non‑transferable and must be displayed on the vehicle’s dashboard at all times; loss or damage must be reported immediately to HR for re‑issuance.
ba1ff7a90137a9e43f8d407d12f254faa8a44ee2:
**Maternity Leave – United Kingdom Office**

The Company provides up to 52 weeks of statutory maternity leave to eligible employees working in the United Kingdom, comprising 26 weeks of Ordinary Maternity Leave followed by an additional 26 weeks of Additional Maternity Leave. Employees are entitled to receive Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) for up to 39 weeks, paid at 90 % of their average weekly earnings for the first 6 weeks and then at the statutory rate (or 90 % of earnings, whichever is lower) for the remaining 33 weeks, provided they meet the qualifying criteria. To qualify, the employee must have been continuously employed by the Company for at least 26 weeks by the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth and must earn at least the lower earnings limit for National Insurance contributions. Employees must notify their line manager and HR in writing of their pregnancy, intended start date of leave, and expected return date no later than the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth. The Company will retain the employee’s position (or a suitable alternative) for the duration of the statutory leave and will consider any additional contractual maternity benefits in accordance with the employee’s individual employment contract.
762a876bf3a3d27991301c0e5fe0b41476bbd0f1:
**Severance Pay Policy**

The Company shall provide severance pay to eligible employees whose employment is terminated without cause, in accordance with the following guidelines: (1) Employees with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service will receive one (1) week of base salary for each full year of service, up to a maximum of twenty‑six (26) weeks; (2) Employees with less than twelve (12) months of service are not eligible for severance pay unless otherwise required by applicable law or a collective bargaining agreement; (3) Severance payments will be made in a lump sum within thirty (30) days of the termination date, subject to all required withholdings and deductions; and (4) The Company reserves the right to modify or discontinue this severance policy at any time, provided that any changes will not affect employees who have already accrued severance entitlement.
f30a2b25f2b37f53dc276e482cb5873c776090a0:
**Password Reset Procedure – Company Email Accounts**  
Employees must reset their company email passwords through the secure Self‑Service Portal located at https://portal.company.com/password‑reset. To initiate a reset, log in with your corporate credentials, select “Email Password Reset,” and follow the on‑screen prompts to verify your identity via multi‑factor authentication. Once verification is complete, you will be prompted to create a new password that meets the company’s complexity requirements (minimum 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special characters). The new password will take effect immediately; you must update any saved credentials on mobile devices or email clients within 24 hours. For assistance, contact the IT Help Desk at ext. 1234 or helpdesk@company.com.
ec2ba5da9ed4f538aba170e0b3f51bb49e1d15fd:
**Employee Referral Bonus Policy**

The Company offers a referral bonus to current employees who refer candidates that are hired into full‑time positions and successfully complete a 90‑day probationary period. The bonus amount is $1,500 for each qualifying referral and will be paid in the first payroll cycle following the new hire’s 90th day of employment. Employees may submit referrals through the designated online portal; only one bonus per candidate is payable, and referrals for positions already posted internally or externally are not eligible. The referral bonus is considered taxable income and will be reported on the employee’s W‑2. All referrals are subject to review and approval by the Human Resources department, which retains final discretion on eligibility and payment.
9bb1c496cc9813651489367925f8f44a58c3f9c8:
**Paid Time Off (PTO) Accrual and Balance**

All full‑time employees accrue PTO at a rate of 1.25 days per month of continuous service, up to a maximum of 15 days (120 hours) per calendar year. Part‑time employees accrue PTO on a pro‑rated basis according to the number of hours worked each month. Employees may view their current PTO balance at any time through the company’s HR portal; the balance reflects all accrued, used, and any forfeited hours as of the date of the query. Unused PTO may be carried over to the following year up to a maximum of 5 days (40 hours); any accrued PTO beyond this limit will be forfeited at year‑end unless a written extension is approved by management.
bf07a1acf00097f6f24bdde9b7bfd0e611f627b7:
**Leave Requests and Scheduling**  
Employees may submit a request for any type of leave at least 10 business days prior to the intended start date, unless the leave is for an unforeseen emergency or a statutory entitlement that requires shorter notice. Requests are reviewed by the employee’s direct supervisor and the Human Resources department to ensure adequate staffing levels and compliance with applicable leave policies. Approval is granted based on operational needs, the employee’s accrued leave balance, and any previously scheduled absences. If the requested leave falls within a peak business period or conflicts with critical project deadlines, the supervisor may propose alternative dates or a partial approval. All approved leave will be documented in the company’s time‑off tracking system and reflected on the employee’s leave balance.
9079cb39a888b764dd54ef1f671395608bcd7c06:
**Reimbursement Limits**  
The Company will reimburse employees for approved business expenses up to a maximum of $500 per calendar month, unless a higher amount is pre‑authorized in writing by a department manager. Expenses exceeding this limit must be submitted with a justification and receive prior approval before reimbursement can be processed. All reimbursement requests must be accompanied by itemized receipts and submitted through the expense management system within 30 days of the incurring date. The Finance Department reserves the right to adjust individual limits based on role, travel frequency, or project requirements, and any such adjustments will be communicated in writing.
5c45b95444b0620b8da9853000e00000395c1041:
**Eligibility for Company Benefits**  
All regular full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of 90 consecutive days of continuous service are eligible to participate in the company’s benefit programs, including health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off. Temporary, part‑time, and contract workers are not eligible for these benefits unless they are specifically designated as “eligible” in a written agreement with Human Resources. Eligibility is automatically confirmed in the employee’s payroll record; any discrepancies must be reported to HR within five business days of the employee’s start date.
85b56c5d8f2347714dbf19e32d518800c3181377:
**Enrollment Procedure**  
Employees may enroll in the company benefits program during the annual Open Enrollment period or within 30 days of a qualifying life event. To enroll, log in to the HR portal, navigate to the “Benefits Enrollment” section, and complete the online enrollment form by selecting the desired plans and confirming your choices. All required documentation must be uploaded through the portal before the submission deadline; incomplete submissions will not be processed. Once submitted, you will receive an electronic confirmation email with a summary of your elected benefits.
7f1b6509d5ec742362b482c5c99c5b2dac7a5ad9:
**Approval Process**  
All requests requiring managerial authorization must be submitted through the company’s electronic workflow system. The employee’s direct supervisor reviews the request first; if approved, it is automatically routed to the department head for secondary approval. Upon receipt of both approvals, the system notifies the employee and records the decision. Any request that is denied at any stage will include a brief rationale and may be resubmitted after the indicated corrective actions are taken.
0182f5068613e395c5ad4f776d8156c49912b7f0:
**Effective Date of Benefits Coverage**  
Coverage under the Company’s health, dental, vision, and life insurance plans commences on the first day of the month following the employee’s successful completion of the mandatory three‑day waiting period after the official hire date. For employees who begin employment on the first day of a month, coverage will start on the first day of the following month. If an employee’s start date falls on a weekend or recognized holiday, the waiting period is calculated from the next regular business day, and coverage will still begin on the first day of the subsequent month. All eligible dependents may be added to the employee’s plan during the open enrollment period or within 30 days of a qualifying life event, with coverage for dependents becoming effective on the same date as the employee’s coverage.
6ed6e4c7804a814a12954bccb609b85eb10be5d7:
**Reimbursement Policy**  
The Company will reimburse employees for reasonable, pre‑approved expenses incurred in the performance of their duties, provided that a valid receipt and a completed Expense Reimbursement Form are submitted within thirty (30) calendar days of the expense. Eligible expenses must be directly related to business activities and conform to the limits outlined in the applicable expense category guidelines. All reimbursement requests are subject to review and approval by the employee’s manager and the Finance Department; expenses that lack proper documentation or fall outside approved categories will not be reimbursed.
